intro.title: Networking Skills
paragraphs: You are sitting in a waiting room outside an interview room, about to attend a startup networking event. The room is long and narrow, like a hallway, with off-white carpet and walls.

Two couches - one yellow, one teal - line the walls with small coffee tables beside them. A coffee machine sits in the corner with paper cups and a trash can nearby. Green plants and a poster on the wall add a touch of life to the space.
Three other people are in the room with you. This could be a great opportunity to practice your networking skills...

dialogues.busy: Sorry, I need to finish up here.
dialogues.default: He seems focused on his laptop.

dialogues.line1_you: Hi, are you here for the startup event?
dialogues.line2_you: What line of work are you in?
dialogues.summary: He didn't seem very interested in talking. The conversation died out quickly. Maybe a different approach would work with someone else.
dialogues.default: He's quietly looking at his phone.

dialogues.line1_you: Hi there! Are you also here for the startup event?
dialogues.line1_her: Yes, I am! I'm Edith. I run a small business incubator downtown. Are you a founder?
dialogues.line2_you: Not yet, but I've been thinking about it. What kind of startups do you work with?
dialogues.line2_her: Mostly early-stage tech and social enterprises. We help with everything from business plans to finding funding. It's very rewarding work.
dialogues.line3_you: That sounds amazing. What got you into that?
dialogues.line3_her: I started my own company years ago and wished I'd had more support. So I built the kind of place I would have wanted. Here, take my card - let's stay in touch!
dialogues.line4_you: Thank you, Edith! I'd love to learn more about your incubator sometime.
dialogues.summary: Great conversation! You made a genuine connection with Edith and exchanged contact information. That's networking done right.
dialogues.buildIntro: Edith walks back over to you with a fresh cup of coffee.
dialogues.build1_her: So, tell me - what really drives you? What's the big idea you've been sitting on?
dialogues.build2a_you: I've been passionate about making education more accessible through technology. What challenges do you see founders face most?
dialogues.build2b_you: Well, I have this app idea that's going to make millions. Let me tell you all about it...
dialogues.build2a_response: That's a wonderful mission! The biggest challenge I see is founders trying to do everything alone. That's exactly why the incubator exists - no one should have to figure it all out by themselves.
dialogues.build2b_response: Oh... that's... ambitious. You know, the most successful founders I've seen are the ones who ask questions, not just pitch.
dialogues.build3_her: Speaking of support, have you thought about what kind of network you'd need to bring your idea to life?
dialogues.build4_her: That's a thoughtful answer. Building a network is really about finding people whose strengths complement yours.
dialogues.build5a_you: What advice would you give someone just starting to build their professional network?
dialogues.build5b_you: I already have a pretty good network, actually. I mostly just need funding.
dialogues.build5a_response: Start by being genuinely curious about other people. Ask about their work, their challenges. Networking isn't about collecting contacts - it's about building relationships where both sides benefit.
dialogues.build5b_response: Hmm, networking is about more than just what you need. The best connections happen when you think about what you can offer, too.
dialogues.build6_her: You know, I've really enjoyed this conversation. It's rare to meet someone who listens as much as they talk. That's a real networking strength.
dialogues.build7a_you: Thank you, Edith. I've learned a lot from talking with you. How can I be helpful to you in return?
dialogues.build7b_you: Thanks! So, about that incubator - can you get me a spot?
dialogues.build7a_response: I appreciate you asking! Actually, we're always looking for fresh perspectives at our mentor nights. Would you be interested in attending one?
dialogues.build7b_response: Ha! I admire the directness, but networking works best when it doesn't feel transactional. Let's build the relationship first.
dialogues.build8_her: Remember - networking is a skill with four parts: Initiate, Build, Maintain, and Leverage. We've covered the first two today. Keep practicing!
dialogues.buildSummary: Excellent work! You've deepened your connection with Edith by asking open questions, showing genuine interest, and thinking about two-way value.

initiate.title: Puzzle 1: Initiate
initiate.instructions: Click on the people in the room to try starting a conversation. Not every attempt will succeed - that's normal in networking!

feedback.npc1Done: He's too busy right now. That's okay - not everyone is available to network at every moment.
feedback.npc2Done: Short, closed answers. Sometimes conversations just don't flow. Don't take it personally.
feedback.edithDone: A great connection! Edith was open, engaged, and you exchanged contact info.
feedback.allComplete: You've tried talking to everyone in the room. You learned that networking requires reading the situation - some people aren't available, some conversations don't click, and sometimes you find a real connection.

mirror.popupContent: No salad between the teeth, check.
mirror.selfReflection: Looking good. But networking isn't just about appearances - it's about being present, being curious, and being genuine. Time to put that into practice.
mirror.edithReturns: You notice Edith coming back from the coffee machine. This could be a good chance to continue the conversation...

build.title: Puzzle 2: Build
build.instructions: Continue your conversation with Edith. When given options, choose the response that builds a genuine, two-way connection.
build.typedPrompt: Edith asks about your network needs. Type your thoughts:

feedback.goodChoice: Good choice! That response shows genuine interest and builds the relationship.
feedback.poorChoice: That response focuses too much on yourself. Try to think about the other person too.
feedback.complete: You've successfully built a deeper relationship with Edith through genuine conversation.

maintain.title: Puzzle 3: Maintain
maintain.instructions: Your phone buzzes with a notification. Time to practice maintaining your network connections through messaging.

fredrik.name: Fredrik
fredrik.incoming: Hey! Great running into you at the event earlier. Want to grab coffee sometime this week?
fredrik.optionA: Absolutely! How about Thursday afternoon? There's a great cafe near the convention center.
fredrik.feedbackA: Great response! Specific and enthusiastic - it shows you value the connection.
fredrik.feedbackB: Too vague. When maintaining contacts, be specific and show genuine interest.

maksym.name: Maksym (former colleague)
maksym.optionA: Hi Maksym, it's been a while! How are you doing? I saw your company just launched a new product - congratulations!
maksym.feedbackA: Perfect! Personal, specific, and shows you've been paying attention to their work.
maksym.feedbackB: Too vague - this message doesn't give them anything to respond to.

iman.name: Iman (event planner)
iman.optionA: Hi Iman! How have you been? Any fun events coming up? I really enjoyed the last one you organized.
iman.optionB: Hey Iman, I need a favor. Can you get me into the next industry mixer?
iman.feedbackA: Well done! You're showing interest in their work before asking for anything.
iman.feedbackB: Too direct and transactional. Build the relationship before asking for favors.

lars.name: Lars (small business owner)
lars.optionA: Hi Lars! I came across an article about sustainable packaging that reminded me of your business. Thought you might find it interesting!
lars.optionB: Hey Lars, I'm looking for new opportunities. Let me know if you hear of anything.
lars.feedbackA: Excellent! Sharing something relevant shows you think about your contacts' interests.
lars.feedbackB: Too self-serving. Maintaining relationships means giving, not just taking.

feedback.allSent: Great job maintaining your network! Remember: good networking maintenance is about showing genuine interest, being specific, and offering value - not just reaching out when you need something.

leverage.title: Puzzle 4: Leverage
leverage.instructions: You've spotted a grant opportunity on the wall poster. Now it's time to leverage your network wisely.
leverage.posterDetails: Grants available: EUR 2,000 - EUR 10,000 for early-stage startups. Application deadline: June 15. Open to all sectors.
leverage.question: This could be a great opportunity! But you'll need help with the application. Who from your network should you reach out to?

options.maksym: Reach out to Maksym (former IT colleague)
options.edith: Reach out to Edith (business incubator manager)
options.lars: Reach out to Lars (small business owner)

explanations.maksym: Maksym is great for IT advice, but grant applications aren't really his area of expertise.
explanations.edith: Edith runs a business incubator that helps startups with exactly this kind of thing - business plans, funding, grants. She's the perfect person to ask!
explanations.iman: Iman is wonderful for events and connections, but grant applications aren't her specialty.
explanations.lars: Lars is a fellow small business owner who might be competing for the same grant. It could create an awkward situation.

feedback.wrong: Think about who in your network has the most relevant expertise for grant applications and startup support.
feedback.correct: Exactly right! Edith's incubator is designed to help startups navigate funding opportunities. Leveraging your network means reaching out to the right person for the right task.

leverage.answerOverlay: The correct answer is: Reach out to Edith. Her business incubator specializes in helping startups with business plans and funding - exactly what you need for a grant application.

hints.initiate: Try clicking on the people in the room to start conversations.
hints.initiateNpc1Done: You've talked to Marcus. Try someone else!
hints.initiateNpc2Done: Try talking to the woman by the coffee machine.
hints.mirror: Look for your bag on the couch - there might be something useful inside.
hints.mirrorReflection: Take a moment to reflect, then look for Edith.
hints.build: Click on Edith to continue your conversation.
hints.buildConversation: Choose the response that shows genuine interest in the other person.
hints.maintain: Check your phone to respond to messages from your contacts.
hints.maintainContacts: Choose responses that show genuine interest and offer value.
hints.leverage: Look at the poster on the wall for an opportunity.
hints.leverageQuestion: Think about which contact has the most relevant expertise for startup grants.
hints.default: Look around the room and interact with the people and objects.

systemDialogues.enterRoom: Okay, here I am. A waiting room full of strangers. Perfect opportunity to practice my networking skills. Let me see who's around...
systemDialogues.npc1Rejection: He's busy. That's fine - knowing when someone isn't available is an important part of networking too.
systemDialogues.npc2Awkward: Well, that was... brief. Sometimes conversations just don't take off. The key is not to give up.
systemDialogues.edithSuccess: That went really well! I got Edith's card and she seemed genuinely interested in staying in touch.
systemDialogues.initiateComplete: I've talked to everyone. Some conversations worked better than others, but I learned something from each one. Networking is about reading the room and finding the right connections.
systemDialogues.mirrorFound: Hmm, my bag is here on the couch. Let me check...
systemDialogues.mirrorClose: Alright, looking presentable. But networking is more than looks - it's about being genuine and curious.
systemDialogues.edithReturns: Oh, Edith is coming back this way. This is a chance to build on that initial connection!
systemDialogues.buildComplete: What a great conversation! I really feel like I've built a genuine connection with Edith. She even invited me to a mentor night.
systemDialogues.phoneNotification: My phone is buzzing. Let me check my messages...
systemDialogues.maintainComplete: Done! Keeping in touch with my network doesn't have to be complicated - it just has to be genuine.
systemDialogues.noticePoster: Hmm, that poster on the wall looks interesting. Let me take a closer look...
systemDialogues.leverageComplete: Smart move. Knowing who to reach out to - and why - is the final piece of the networking puzzle.
systemDialogues.congratulations: Congratulations! You've mastered all four networking skills: Initiate, Build, Maintain, and Leverage. Time to put them into practice in the real world!

popupContent: No salad between the teeth, check.

completion.title: Congratulations!
completion.message: You have successfully completed the Networking Skills escape room! You've learned and practiced the four key networking skills: Initiate (starting conversations), Build (deepening connections), Maintain (staying in touch), and Leverage (using your network wisely). These skills will serve you well in your professional journey!
completion.revealedNote: That one needed the answer shown, so it is worth going over this part in the module.
